title: TransportConfig
description:
Wyrd client transport selection.

gRPC is the default. Variants for queue transports (Kafka, RabbitMQ, Redis) are intentionally absent in this phase.

Wire shape: `{"transport": "grpc", "params": { ... }}`.

oneOf.description: HTTP transport (reqwest). Secondary path for gRPC-restricted environments.
In-memory loopback transport for tests. Always available.

GrpcConfig.description:
Configuration for the gRPC transport.

gRPC is the default transport for `wyrd-client`. The server-side endpoint is the Wyrd ingest gateway (`vala-ingest`, PR4.2) or any compatible tonic-based receiver.

This config carries transport wiring only. Authentication is owned by `AuthMiddleware`, which injects the `x-wyrd-access-token` credential per call; there is no auth field here.

connect_retries.description:
Connection-level retry budget. The transport retries the initial connection up to this many times before surfacing an error.

Default: [`GRPC_DEFAULT_CONNECT_RETRIES`] (`3`).

endpoint.description:
gRPC server endpoint. Must be `http://host:port` (plaintext) or `https://host:port` (TLS). Must be non-empty.

Default: [`GRPC_DEFAULT_ENDPOINT`] (`"http://localhost:50051"`).

keepalive_interval_ms.description:
HTTP/2 keepalive ping interval in milliseconds. `0` disables pings.

Default: [`GRPC_DEFAULT_KEEPALIVE_INTERVAL_MS`] (`20_000`, 20 s).

keepalive_timeout_ms.description:
HTTP/2 keepalive ping timeout in milliseconds. The connection is closed if the peer does not respond within this window.

Default: [`GRPC_DEFAULT_KEEPALIVE_TIMEOUT_MS`] (`5_000`, 5 s).

max_message_bytes.description:
Maximum gRPC message size in bytes (both encoding and decoding).

Default: [`GRPC_DEFAULT_MAX_MESSAGE_BYTES`] (`4_194_304`, 4 MiB).

timeout_ms.description:
Per-call timeout in milliseconds.

Default: [`GRPC_DEFAULT_TIMEOUT_MS`] (`30_000`, 30 s).

tls.description: Optional TLS configuration. When `None`, connections use the scheme in `endpoint` to decide TLS (`https://` implies TLS with the system CA pool, `http://` means plaintext).

HttpConfig.description:
Configuration for the HTTP transport.

The HTTP transport is a fallback for environments where gRPC is unavailable or blocked. Ingest routes are appended by the client at call time; `base_url` is the common prefix.

This config carries transport wiring only. Authentication is owned by `AuthMiddleware`, which injects the `x-wyrd-access-token` credential per call; there is no auth field here.

base_url.description:
Base URL for all ingest routes. Must be non-empty. Ingest routes (`/api/v1/observations`, `/api/v1/records`, etc.) are appended at call time.

Example: `"https://wyrd-ingest.example.com"`. Default: [`HTTP_DEFAULT_BASE_URL`] (`"http://localhost:50050"`).

compression.description:
Whether to gzip-compress request bodies. Useful for high-volume payloads; the server must accept `Content-Encoding: gzip`.

Default: `false`.

timeout_ms.description:
Request timeout in milliseconds.

Default: [`HTTP_DEFAULT_TIMEOUT_MS`] (`30_000`, 30 s).

tls.description: Optional TLS configuration. When `None`, the system CA pool is used and the scheme in `base_url` governs whether TLS is active.

MockConfig.description:
Configuration for the mock (in-memory loopback) transport.

Use this transport in unit tests where you want to assert what was published without touching a network. `wyrd-client::transport::mock` records every flushed envelope into an in-memory buffer keyed by [`MockConfig::label`] and provides `mock::drain(label)` to retrieve flushed records.

The mock transport is always available in `wyrd-client` (no feature gate). `MockConfig::fail_on_drain` lets tests inject deterministic drain failures — a Wyrd-native addition the predecessor mock did not support.

# Default

`MockConfig::default()` returns `{ label: "default", fail_on_drain: None }`. The default is a working config — it does not need `validate()` and is safe to use directly in tests that do not care about label isolation.

fail_on_drain.description: Inject a drain failure. When `Some(n)`, the `nth` call to drain returns `Err`; all other calls succeed normally. Counting starts from 1 (i.e. `Some(1)` fails the first drain). `None` means the mock always succeeds.

label.description: Buffer label. Multiple `MockConfig` instances with the same label share the same in-memory buffer in `wyrd-client::transport::mock`. Use distinct labels to isolate test scenarios running in the same process.

SecretRef.description: Pointer into a Wyrd runtime secret source. Production builds support environment variables, mounted files, and external secret-manager keys.

oneOf.description:
An environment variable name. The runtime reads `std::env::var(name)` at connect time. Conventionally `SCREAMING_SNAKE_CASE`.

Example: `{"source": "env", "name": "WYRD_SECRET_API_KEY"}`.

name.description: Environment variable name. Must be non-empty.

oneOf.description:
An absolute path to a file on the local filesystem. Kubernetes Secret volume mounts land here.

Example: `{"source": "file", "path": "/var/run/secrets/wyrd/api-key"}`.

path.description: Absolute path to a file whose contents are the secret value. Must be non-empty.

oneOf.description:
A backend-agnostic key in an external secret manager (HashiCorp Vault, AWS Secrets Manager, Google Secret Manager). The Wyrd auth shell maps the key to the configured backend.

Example: `{"source": "vault", "key": "secret/data/wyrd/api-key"}`.

key.description: Backend-agnostic key path. Interpretation is backend-specific.

TlsConfig.description:
TLS configuration for a transport connection.

All certificate fields are optional; an absent field means "use the system default / skip that verification step". Setting `insecure_skip_verify` to `true` disables peer certificate validation and SHOULD NOT be used outside local development.

ca_cert.description: PEM-encoded CA certificate bundle. When set, overrides the system CA pool for this connection.

client_cert.description: PEM-encoded client certificate for mTLS. Must be paired with `client_key`.

client_key.description: PEM-encoded client private key for mTLS. Must be paired with `client_cert`.

insecure_skip_verify.description:
Disable peer certificate verification. Defaults to `false`.

**WARNING:** setting this to `true` opens the connection to man-in-the-middle attacks. Use only in local development.

server_name_override.description: Override the server name used in SNI and certificate verification. Useful when the server's certificate CN does not match the address in `endpoint`.
